subject: chemistry
title: The mole and the Avogadro constant
key_idea: A mole is a fixed number of particles: 6.02 × 10²³, the Avogadro constant. One mole of a substance has a mass in grams equal to its relative formula mass. This links mass, moles and number of particles.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) Chemists count particles in moles because atoms are far too small to count one by one.

items.meaning: The unit for the amount of a substance. One mole contains the Avogadro constant number of particles.
The number of atoms, molecules or ions in one mole: 6.02 × 10²³ per mole.

items: One mole of any substance contains the same number of particles as one mole of any other substance.
The particles can be atoms, molecules, ions, electrons or formulae.
One mole of carbon atoms has the same number of atoms as the number of molecules in one mole of carbon dioxide.
The mass of one mole in grams is numerically equal to the relative formula mass (Mr). One mole of carbon dioxide, with Mr 44, has a mass of 44 g.
One mole is 6.02 × 10²³ particles of any type.
The mass of one mole in grams equals Mr (or Ar for an element).

blocks.text: (Higher tier) The mass of a sample, its Mr and the amount in moles are linked by one equation.

blocks.label: Number of moles
where: number of moles is in mol.
Mr is the relative formula mass, or Ar for an atom.

items.text: Convert kilograms or milligrams to grams first. 14.52 kg = 14 520 g.
For ammonium nitrate, Mr = 80, so 14 520 ÷ 80 = 181.5 mol.
In standard form to 2 significant figures this is 1.8 × 10².

items: To find a mass, rearrange: mass = number of moles × Mr.
Use the Mr of the particle you are counting. For oxygen gas, O₂, Mr = 32. For oxygen atoms, Ar = 16.

diagram.alt: Calculate the number of moles from a mass and a relative formula mass.
diagram.question: Calculate the number of moles in {m} g of a substance with a relative formula mass of {mr}. Give your answer to 3 decimal places.

items: Moles = mass ÷ Mr. Mass = moles × Mr.
Work in grams. Convert kg and mg first.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) Multiply moles by the Avogadro constant to find the number of particles. Answers are usually in standard form.

blocks.label: Number of particles
blocks.formula: number of particles = number of moles × 6.02 × 10²³
where: number of moles is in mol.
6.02 × 10²³ is the Avogadro constant, per mole.

items.text: 72 g of water, Mr = 18, is 72 ÷ 18 = 4 mol.

items: To go the other way, divide the number of particles by 6.02 × 10²³ to get moles.
Mass of one atom = Ar ÷ (6.02 × 10²³) grams. For chromium (Ar = 52.0) this is 8.64 × 10⁻²³ g.
Be clear what the particle is. A mole of oxygen molecules, O₂, has twice as many oxygen atoms as molecules.

diagram.alt: Calculate the number of particles from moles.
diagram.question: Calculate the number of atoms in {n} mol of an element. Give your answer as a number to be multiplied by 10²³, so 7.5 means 7.5 × 10²³ atoms. (Avogadro constant = 6.02 × 10²³ per mole)
working: number of atoms = number of moles × 6.02 × 10²³

items: For particles from a mass: mass to moles first, then moles to particles.
Never multiply a mass directly by the Avogadro constant.

checks.q: What is meant by the Avogadro constant?
checks.a: The number of particles (atoms, molecules or ions) in one mole of a substance. It is 6.02 × 10²³ per mole.

checks.q: Calculate the number of moles in 101 g of neon. (Ar of Ne = 20.2)
Calculate the number of gold atoms in 3.94 g of gold. (Ar of Au = 197; Avogadro constant = 6.02 × 10²³)

mistakes.right: Convert the mass to grams first. 14.52 kg = 14 520 g, so 14 520 ÷ 80 = 181.5 mol.

mistakes.wrong: 181.5 mol, when the question asks for standard form to 2 significant figures.
mistakes.right: The last mark is for the form asked: 1.8 × 10² mol.

mistakes.wrong: Number of C₇₀ molecules from 1 mole of carbon atoms = 1 × 6.02 × 10²³.
mistakes.right: Each molecule has 70 atoms. Moles of C₇₀ = 1 ÷ 70, then multiply by 6.02 × 10²³ to give 8.6 × 10²¹.

worked_example.question:
A bag of fertiliser contains 14.52 kg of ammonium nitrate (NH₄NO₃).

Relative formula mass (Mr): NH₄NO₃ = 80

Calculate the number of moles of ammonium nitrate in the bag of fertiliser.

Give your answer in standard form to 2 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: An answer of 1.8 × 10² mol gains all 4 marks. The Mr given (80) must be used.

mistakes.right: Convert mass to moles first: 0.11 ÷ 44 = 0.0025 mol. Then multiply by 6.02 × 10²³.
Convert milligrams to grams first: 74 mg = 0.074 g. Using 74 directly gives an answer 1000 times too big and loses marks.

mistakes.wrong: Number of gold atoms in 3.94 g = 3.94 ÷ 197 = 0.02 atoms.
mistakes.right: 0.02 is the number of moles, not atoms. Multiply by 6.02 × 10²³ to get 1.2 × 10²² atoms.

worked_example.question:
Calculate the number of molecules in 0.11 g of carbon dioxide.

Give your answer to two significant figures.

(relative formula mass: CO₂ = 44; Avogadro constant = 6.02 × 10²³)
worked_example.tip: An answer of 1.5 × 10²¹ scores 3 marks with or without working.

exam_phrases: mass of one atom of chromium = 52 ÷ 6.02 × 10²³

mistakes.wrong: Number of water molecules in 72 g = 72 × 6.02 × 10²³.
mistakes.right: This scores 0. Find the moles first: 72 ÷ 18 = 4. Then 4 × 6.02 × 10²³.

mistakes.wrong: The Avogadro constant is the number of atoms in one mole of an element.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. It is the number of entities in one mole. If you say atoms or molecules, link it to a correct substance.

mistakes.wrong: Mass of one atom of chromium = 9 × 10⁻²³ g.
mistakes.right: Do not round to 1 significant figure. Give 8.64 × 10⁻²³ g.

worked_example.question:
The value of the Avogadro constant is 6.02 × 10²³.

Calculate the number of water molecules in 72 g of water, H₂O.

Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: 2.41 × 10²⁴ on the answer line scores 3 marks. The Mr of water is 18.
